root_cause.text: In batman-adv fragment reassembly, the chain’s accumulated payload length was stored in a 16-bit `u16` field and updated with plain addition, so large fragment chains could overflow/truncate `chain->size` and bypass the size validation used before reassembly.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `struct batadv_frag_table_entry.size` from `u16` to `size_t`, adds `check_add_overflow(chain->size, data_len, &chain->size)` in `batadv_frag_insert_packet()`, and explicitly says the existing accounting “allows the accumulated fragment length to be truncated during updates,” letting malformed fragment chains bypass validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the overflow utility header so the file can use kernel overflow-checking helpers.
intent_record.what: A new include directive was added: `#include <linux/overflow.h>`.
intent_record.how: This makes overflow-checking helpers and related macros available in this compilation unit, enabling later code in the file to use kernel-safe arithmetic overflow detection.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change batadv_frag_size_limit() to use size_t for size calculations and return type consistency.
intent_record.what: The return type of batadv_frag_size_limit() was changed from int to size_t, and its local variable limit was changed from int to size_t while keeping the same arithmetic with BATADV_FRAG_MAX_FRAG_SIZE, sizeof(struct batadv_frag_packet), and BATADV_FRAG_MAX_FRAGMENTS.
intent_record.how: This makes the function compute and return the fragmentation payload limit using an unsigned size type that better matches a size calculation, avoiding signed integer semantics and potential truncation or signed overflow issues when the value is used as a byte size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add local state for overflow tracking and data length handling in fragment packet insertion logic.
intent_record.what: In `batadv_frag_insert_packet()`, two new local variables were added: a `bool overflow = false;` and a `size_t data_len;` declaration, inserted alongside the existing `frag_packet`, `bucket`, `seqno`, `hdr_size`, and `ret` variables.
intent_record.how: By introducing these variables, the function is prepared to track an overflow condition and to store a packet data length value during fragment insertion/validation logic, which can affect later control flow and size calculations at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Compute and store the fragment payload length early so packet reassembly logic uses the correct data size.
intent_record.what: A new assignment `data_len = skb->len - hdr_size;` was added immediately after `frag_packet` is set from `skb->data` and before `seqno` is read.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now computes the payload length from the packet length and header size before continuing with fragment processing. This makes the `data_len` value available for later logic in the function, likely ensuring fragment bookkeeping or validation uses the correct payload size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix fragment chain size initialization to use the validated data length.
intent_record.what: In `batadv_frag_insert_packet()`, the assignment to `chain->size` was changed from `skb->len - hdr_size` to `data_len` when initializing a new fragment chain.
intent_record.how: This makes the fragment chain size track the computed payload length directly instead of recalculating it from the skb length and header size, which can prevent incorrect size accounting if those values differ.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add overflow-safe fragment chain size accounting to prevent wraparound when inserting packets.
intent_record.what: In the fragment insertion path, the code no longer directly increments `chain->size` by `skb->len - hdr_size` when inserting before an existing fragment. Instead, it adds a `check_add_overflow(chain->size, data_len, &chain->size)` call and sets `overflow = true` if the addition overflows.
intent_record.how: This changes fragment chain accounting to detect and handle integer overflow when updating the accumulated chain size. At runtime, it prevents `chain->size` from silently wrapping around on oversized or malicious inputs, allowing the code to mark the chain as overflowed instead of maintaining a corrupted size value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add overflow detection to fragment chain size accounting and reject chains that overflow during accumulation.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct increment of `chain->size` with an overflow-checked addition using `check_add_overflow(chain->size, data_len, &chain->size)`, setting a new `overflow` flag if the addition overflows. It also updates the later validation شرط to clear the chain when `overflow` is true, in addition to the existing size-limit and total-size checks.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the fragment chain size is now accumulated safely even when the new fragment length would exceed the range of the size field. If the arithmetic overflows, the chain is marked invalid and rejected during the post-insert sanity check, preventing silent wraparound and incorrect acceptance of oversized fragment chains.

intent_record.intent_summary: Widen the fragment size accumulator to prevent overflow when tracking assembled packet sizes.
intent_record.what: In struct batadv_frag_table_entry, the type of the size field was changed from u16 to size_t; the field name and surrounding structure definition were otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: This allows the accumulated packet size to be stored in a wider integer type, preventing truncation or overflow when the total buffered fragment size exceeds 16 bits and making the size tracking safe on larger packets or architectures.
